Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team had a couple of follow-ups after reviewing the SIG draft you sent over. Two specific asks: 1) Clarify the default retention for prompt and response logs that pass through Redwood Hosted API (we saw references to ephemeral caches in the docs but want the concrete retention windows), and 2) Confirm whether customer prompt/response data is ever used to train Redwood models or otherwise material for model updates.

We also need a short statement we can include in our vendor-risk repo that says whether MedSentry customer data is excluded from training and, if not, what opt-outs you provide.

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers below; I'll follow up with a packaged PDF and our SOC 2 excerpt for your repo.

1) Retention windows (hosted API):
- Request/response logs: default 30 days for enabled audit logs; 7 days for transient telemetry used solely for runtime optimization.
- KV/prefix cache (ephemeral): kept only in memory for the lifetime of the session; no persistent write by default.

2) Training on customer data:
- Redwood does not use individual customer production data to train or improve our base models by default.
- Exception: explicit, written opt-in only — e.g., a separate agreement where a customer grants permission and provides data for benchmarking/training.

I'll loop in Laura from Legal to confirm wording we can put in a vendor-risk repo. Expect the formal PDF (short statement + related evidence) within 48 hours.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Karthik / Marissa — reviewed. Suggested formal language below that Legal is comfortable with for a vendor-risk repository and for inclusion in the SIG response PDF: please use exactly this wording when we send to MedSentry.

"Redwood Inference Data Handling Statement (short form):
- Redwood Inference does not use customer production prompts, responses, or other content transmitted via our Hosted API to train, improve, or fine-tune our base or service models, unless a customer has provided explicit, documented consent via a separate agreement.
- By default, request/response logs used for troubleshooting and audit are retained for up to 30 days. Short-term telemetry used only for runtime optimization (e.g., scheduling/latency metrics and ephemeral KV cache traces) is retained for up to 7 days and is not stored long-term.
- Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments can configure longer retention or turn off hosted audit logs entirely; such configurations are captured in the customer's deployment agreement.

This language is cleared for vendor-repo inclusion. If MedSentry needs a signed attestation, let me know and Legal will prepare a one-page attestation on company letterhead.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
